title: Jurisdiction-aware audit fabric — PRD sketch
body:
Purpose:
This sketch defines a lightweight PRD for a "jurisdiction-aware audit fabric" for Redwood Private deployments. The goal is to provide customers operating in multiple legal jurisdictions with deterministic, auditable change records that respect per-tenant retention rules, legal-hold requests, and evidentiary packaging requirements while minimizing storage and retrieval cost.

Problem statement:
Customers deploying Private (VPC/on-prem) often have differing legal obligations for how long audit data must be retained, what proof is admissible in their region, and which subset of telemetry is allowed to leave their control plane. Current options are one-size-fits-all: long-term full retention (expensive), or aggressive trimming (risky for compliance and forensics). We need a flexible fabric that:
- Applies per-tenant jurisdictional retention policies (EU, US, APAC variants)
- Produces compact cryptographic artifacts (signed digests, merkle roots) that allow reconstruction / verification of relevant events without storing full payloads forever
- Supports legal-hold overrides and selective un-deletion with auditing of who lifted/created holds
- Operates in private networks (no mandatory cloud egress) and supports on-prem signing (customer KMS / HSM)

Objectives / success metrics:
- Product objective: give customers a way to meet region-specific retention & evidentiary needs without doubling storage costs.
- Success metrics (first 6 months):
  - 90% of evaluated enterprise customers can express their retention policy via UI or API templates
  - 40–60% reduction in long-term storage for typical customer telemetry profiles via compaction + proof layering
  - Ability to produce a verifiable audit bundle for any 30-day window within policy 99% of the time within 30s (on Dedicated hardware)
  - Legal-hold workflows exercised in staging for 3 sample customers without data leakage incidents

Personas / primary users:
- Platform Ops (customer): defines retention policies, legal-hold toggles, and responds to e-discovery requests.
- Security / GRC: validates integrity of audit artifacts, requests full snapshots for investigations.
- Redwood SRE / Solutions Eng: assists in onboarding, verifying proof generation, diagnosing retrieval issues.

Out of scope (for the sketch):
- Full implementation of a regulatory compliance audit assistant (that remains a future product).
- Extensive UI polish — initial surfaces can be form-driven and API-first.

High-level approach (fabric concept):
1) Event tiering and fast-paths:
   - Ingested events are categorized at write-time into tiers: transient (debug traces, short ttl), operational (authz, control-plane changes, 90–365d), forensic (immutable evidence, 1–10y depending on jurisdiction).
   - Default tiering heuristics shipped; customers may override per-route.
2) Compact proof layering:
   - During retention roll-ups, raw payloads older than retention_protect_window are compacted into cryptographic proofs: we store a canonicalized representation and a per-day merkle root, and optionally an encrypted compressed snapshot retained in cold storage.
   - All merkle roots are signed by the signing key (customer-managed KMS when available; Redwood signing key only if customer opts in).
3) Jurisdictional policy engine:
   - A policy language (YAML/JSON templates) that specifies retention windows by event tag, allowed export/egress, legal-hold constraints, and required proof levels (e.g., signed merkle root + snapshot vs signed digest only).
4) Legal-hold & e-discovery APIs:
   - API to create a legal-hold on an entity (tenant, route, resource path) with metadata (issuer, justification, expiration if any).
   - Legal-hold prevents compaction/deletion and creates an immutable record of the hold creation and release, themselves signed and versioned.
5) Evidence bundle generation:
   - On-demand bundle API returns a signed, time-stamped evidence packet that contains either raw events (if still stored), or a verifiable chain describing how to reconstruct/verify events using stored snapshots + merkle branches.

Data model (flat view):
- audit_event: {timestamp, tenant_id, route, actor, action_type, payload_digest, event_tags}
- daily_root: {date, tenant_id, merkle_root, signer_key_id, signature}
- hold_record: {hold_id, tenant_id, created_by, created_at, scope, justification, status, signature}
Note: actual PRD will expand schema fields; above is intentionally flat for readability.

API sketches (API-first, examples):
- POST /api/v1/retention-policy (body: policy template) => 200 (id)
- GET /api/v1/retention-policy/{id} => policy JSON
- POST /api/v1/legal-hold (body: {scope, reason, created_by}) => hold_id
- POST /api/v1/evidence-bundle (body: {tenant, start_ts, end_ts, level: [raw|proof]}) => presigned download link or streaming tar.gz

Security & key management:
- Default mode: Redwood signs merkle roots (useful for hosted convenience).
- Enterprise mode: prefer customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) — keys may never leave customer boundary in on-prem mode.
- Key rotation: record key id in daily_root; previous roots remain verifiable via archived public keys.
- Minimal metadata leakage: evidence bundles strip PII if policy requires; any content that would leave a customer boundary must be explicit and auditable.

Cost model / storage strategy:
- Keep hot logs for short retention window (default 30d) with immediate query access.
- After hot window: compact to proofs and optionally encrypted cold snapshots (S3 Glacier-style).
- Provide savings estimator for customers based on their event rates and chosen proof depth.

Migration / operator experience:
- Tooling: one-off migration job to scaffold default daily_roots for prior history, with sampling to avoid huge up-front costs.
- Rollout: start with enabling proof-layering for non-critical tenants and opt-in for legal-hold enforcement in pilot.

Observability & SLOs:
- SLOs: evidence-bundle generation for last-30d window: p95 < 15s (dedicated pool), p99 < 60s.
- Metrics: compaction savings, failed-verification-rate, legal-hold churn, key-rotation failures, per-tenant retention-policy mismatches.
- Auditability: every admin action (policy change, hold create/release, key rotation) emits signed admin_event linked into the fabric.

Edge cases and open questions (decision items):
- Q1: Acceptable default for customer vs Redwood signing? (Security + sales tradeoff.)
- Q2: How to efficiently support right-to-be-forgotten requests where a merkle root implicitly includes a deleted object's digest? Potential approach: issue a new merkle root epoch that replays without the deleted item and store a redaction proof.
- Q3: Archive encryption key custody model for long-term cold snapshots (customer-only, Redwood escrow, split-key?).

Acceptance criteria for beta:
- Policy language implemented and load-tested on synthetic workloads.
- Evidence bundle API returns verifiable proof for a 90-day window for pilot customers.
- KMS integration for at least AWS and a mock HSM for on-prem testing.
- Operator tooling for emergency-release (with strong authz and audit) and a simple UI surfacing holds and pending releases.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (experiments): implement compaction + merkle root signing in a sandbox; validate proof verification library.
- Phase 1 (pilot): enable for 3 enterprise customers in Dedicated mode (customer KMS optional). Test e-discovery and legal-hold flows.
- Phase 2 (general availability): UI surfaces, cost estimator, region jurisdiction presets, and runbook for SREs.

Appendix — informal notes / rationale:
- We favor "proof layering" over storing everything forever. It reduces cost while preserving verifiability.
- Design must assume some customers will never allow Redwood-managed signing; we should make that path friction-minimal.
- The policy language should be intentionally small and extensible; start with retention + egress + proof-level, iterate based on legal/customer feedback.

Open action items (owners):
- Legal to draft jurisdiction presets (EU/UK/US/CA/APAC) — owner: Priya Nair — due 2025-11-20.
- Infra to prototype merkle root signer + offline verification tool — owner: Liam O'Connor — due 2025-12-15.
- Solutions Eng to scoping pilot customers and test cases — owner: Mateo Alvarez — due 2026-01-10.

Notes to reviewers:
This is intentionally an API-first sketch with emphasis on low initial UI investment. Looking for feedback on the policy primitives, signing/key custody tradeoffs, and proposed SLOs.
